Source deployments and functions Cloud Run deployments from source and functions operate as Cloud Run services and are billed accordingly based on the conditions above. When deploying from source or creating a function, Cloud Run uses Cloud Build to convert your source code or function into an executable image. The images are created in Cloud Build and stored in Artifact Registry. Artifact Registry has its own free tier of storage . If you deploy your source code or function to Artifact Registry and exceed the Artifact Registry free tier usage, you will incur charges for deploying your functions, even when your use of Cloud Run falls within the free tier. Pricing for Cloud Build and Artifact Registry is not included in Cloud Run pricing. To review pricing for these services, see the Cloud Build Pricing and Artifact Registry Pricing pages. Cloud Run uses Eventarc for event delivery. Pricing for Eventarc is not included in the Cloud Run pricing above. Review pricing on the Eventarc Pricing page. Volume discounts Usage discounts on Northflank Cloud and BYOC as your spend grows. Questions Contact us What’s included in the free Sandbox? Up to $20 a month of free resources on Northflank Cloud, across 2 services, 2 jobs, and 1 database. You can also connect one BYOC cluster and use up to 12 vCPU and 48 GB of memory on it; your cloud provider still bills you for that infrastructure. Do you charge per seat? No. Every plan includes unlimited users, deployments, and workloads. You only pay for the compute you run. How is bring your own cloud billed? Northflank bills only for the vCPU on the nodes it manages in your cluster, by the second. Your cloud provider bills the infrastructure directly, so your existing credits and commitments still apply. What forms of payment do you accept? Payments are handled by Stripe and we accept Visa, Mastercard, and American Express. How does consumption based pricing work? You’ll be billed at the end of your monthly billing cycle based on your configured resources and instances, prorated to the second of usage. Read our terms of service for more details. Estimates are exclusive of VAT and GST. Will taxes be included in my monthly invoice? We’re required by law to collect taxes in some countries. Am I charged when I enter my credit card? No — when you enter a card we only verify the card. Your card is only charged at the end of the billing cycle. What currency will I be charged in? You will be charged in US dollars. Start free. Scale when you’re ready Start free on Northflank Cloud or in your own cloud account. Same platform and workflow either way. Modal bills you during application load time and during the time your container is processing inputs. By default, we keep containers alive for 60 seconds after the last inputs before we shut them down, which we also bill for. However, this timeout length is configurable. Once your application has scaled down to zero containers you no longer get charged. How are CPU and memory usage metered? Modal continuously records CPU and memory consumption. CPU usage is tracked in terms of fractional physical cores, allowing for higher utilization compared to providers that set minimum thresholds for core charges. Note that each physical core is equivalent to 2 vCPUs as offered by AWS or GCP. You'll be charged based on whichever is higher: the amount you request or the amount you actually use. Each container has a minimum request of 128 MiB of memory and 0.125 CPU cores, which you can increase if you need more resources. Why are Sandboxes and Functions billed at different CPU and memory rates? Modal Sandboxes are priced at the rate of non-preemptible Functions . Modal Functions are subject to preemption by default; while interruptions are rare, they can happen. CPU Sandboxes, on the other hand, are not subject to preemption. On Modal, a 3x multiplier is applied to the CPU and Memory list price for non-preemptible resources. How does serverless pricing differ from traditional on-demand pricing? Modal's serverless pricing can't be directly compared to traditional on-demand or spot instance pricing. Traditional cloud compute doesn't have instant spin-up times. You might spend 10+ minutes provisioning an instance and another 5 terminating it. You also have to commit to a minimum usage time per instance, usually between 1 minute and 1 hour. All this time is billable. In contrast, Modal spins containers up and down in 1-2 seconds. You don't commit to any minimum usage time per instance. Even though our per-hour prices may sometimes appear higher, your overall costs are lower if your request volumes are spiky or unpredictable. Modal autoscales fast, so you pay for significantly less non-execution time versus traditional compute. You also save on cost by not having to over-provision compute to handle peak loads. What's an example of real-world CPU billing? You schedule a job to run once a day for an hour. The job uses 50% of one CPU core and 256 MiB of memory. This job will cost $0.02365/day for the CPU, and $0.00200/day for the memory, adding up to $0.02565/day , or $0.77 over 30 days . What's an example of real-world GPU billing? You run stable diffusion on an A10G GPU. This will run for about 1.5 seconds to generate each image, while using 4 GiB RAM and 1 CPU. This will cost approximately $0.000458/image in GPU charges, $0.000020/image in CPU charges, and $0.000013/image in memory charges, adding up to $0.000491/image in total charges, i.e., $0.491 per 1,000 images . How should I estimate the total cost of Modal Sandboxes? Because Modal Sandboxes are billed based on active resources, you should estimate total cost differently than you would with other Sandbox providers who charge based on fixed reservations. For CPU, you can estimate by calculating: Sandbox duration × rate × average CPU cores used. For memory, you can estimate by calculating: Sandbox duration × rate × average GiB used. It's important to use the average resource consumption instead of the peak because Modal Sandboxes are charged based on the max(request, usage). For most Modal Sandboxes, the guidance is to not request any resources, defaulting to a small reservation of 0.125 cores and 128 MiB of memory. Modal Sandboxes are designed to burst above their reservation as needed. Since Sandboxes typically have bursty resource consumption, the difference between peak usage and average usage can be significant. Calculating the price of Modal Sandboxes by using peak resource consumption will usually significantly overestimate the total cost. Do I need to purchase credits? Workspaces receive a free allotment of compute per month, but usage on the Starter and Team plans is pay-as-you-go and does not require pre-purchasing compute or tokens. If you want to limit your monthly spend, you can set a Workspace budget . Can I add more than three team members on the starter plan? The starter plan allows up to three users in a workspace. Upgrading to the team plan unlocks an unlimited number of seats. What kinds of applications can I deploy using Modal? You can deploy any application that can be containerized, using Python. Modal is especially well-suited for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from horizontal scaling. This includes ML inference at scale, model training & fine-tuning, data pipelines, numerical & scientific computing, compute-heavy job queues, and much more. Can I use my AWS, GCP, or Azure credits on Modal? At the moment, credits from AWS, GCP, or Azure cannot be applied towards your Modal usage. However, we have a special partnership with AWS that allows eligible startups to unlock additional Modal credits if they are part of AWS Activate. To find out if your company is eligible, please apply to our startup credits program. What does my included usage cover? Included usage applies to compute: Functions and Sandboxes, billed by the second for CPU, memory, and GPU time. Volumes include up to 1 TiB free. It does not apply to Shared Endpoints, which are billed per token rather than per second. Token usage is always billed, starting from your first request. To cap out-of-pocket charges, see spend limits . I'm on the Starter plan. Why am I being charged? Starter has no monthly fee and includes $30 of compute (GPUs, CPUs, Memory) per month. You're billed when you exceed that, or when you use something the included compute doesn't cover. Free usage of Shared Endpoints is not part of the Starter plan. Tokens are billed from your first request, so they will appear on your invoice even if you haven't used your full $30 of included compute. This took effect September 1, 2026. $10 +($5 ✕ read regions) Custom Request price Free $0.2 per 100K No per-command pricing Custom Storage price Free $0.25 per GB - Custom Bandwidth price Free Free - Custom Start Now Start Now Start Now Learn More FAQ How can I upgrade to pay as you go from free tier? Once you enter your credit card, your database will be upgraded to the pay-as-you-go plan and limits will be updated. What is included in free tier? Free tier includes 250MB data size and 500K commands per month. Can I get a free Redis database without signing up? Yes. Send a POST request to https://upstash.com/start-redis and you get a free Redis database instantly, with no signup, credit card, or API key. The response is markdown with credentials and a quickstart, so AI agents can start using it right away. The database is deleted after 3 days unless you claim it into your account from the console link in the response. Once claimed, it follows the pricing on this page. Are paid databases' first 250MB data and 500K commands free? No. Once you upgrade to a paid tier, you will be charged for data size and commands according to that plan. How does the budget work? Budget is only available for the pay-as-you-go plan. You can set a maximum monthly budget for your database so you won't be charged beyond that limit. We send email notifications when you reach 70% and 90% of your monthly budget so you can adjust the limit or upgrade to a Fixed plan. If your usage exceeds the budget cap, your database will be rate limited and your total cost will not exceed the chosen budget. If you change from a Fixed plan to pay-as-you-go mid-month, your budget only tracks your pay-as-you-go spending. Do Fixed plans have command count pricing or limits? Fixed plans have no command-count billing. You pay for data size, bandwidth, and throughput limits, not per command. Are all Redis commands counted in billing? Operational commands like AUTH, HELLO, SELECT, COMMAND, CONFIG, INFO, PING, RESET, and QUIT are not charged. Are databases faster in higher plans? Ops/sec limits are the same in the initial plans, while higher plans increase throughput and other limits. There is no performance difference between plans as long as you stay within the limits. Are read and write commands same price? Yes. But for Global databases, the write commands are replicated to all read regions in addition to the primary region. Replications are also counted as commands. For example, if you have one primary and one read region, 100K writes cost $0.4 ($0.2 x 2). How is the storage cost calculated? For each database, the first 1GB is free. Beyond that, storage is charged at $0.25 per GB of total storage. Total storage is determined by adding up the storage at all replicas and regions. Even if you do not access your data, it still needs to stay persistent in the cloud provider's block storage for durability and high availability. To calculate storage cost, we take the daily average of your total data size across replicas and regions and apply the monthly rate at the end of the month. If you use your database as a cache, setting a timeout with EXPIRE is a good way to minimize cost. What happens when I hit limits on pay-as-you-go plan? We send email notifications when limits are exceeded. We do our best to keep your database running, but we may rate limit depending on the case. Requests above the max request size are rejected with an exception. Collections that exceed the max record size stop accepting new records. Bandwidth and storage do not have hard limits, but you can use a budget limit to avoid unexpected charges. What happens when I hit limits on Fixed plans? We send email notifications when limits are exceeded. If your database hits the bandwidth or storage limits and auto-upgrade is enabled, it upgrades to the next tier. If auto-upgrade is not enabled, the database is rate limited: traffic is blocked for bandwidth cases and write operations are blocked for storage cases. Requests above the max request size are rejected with an exception. Collections that exceed the max record size stop accepting new records. Are there free trials? Yes, we can provide free trials for testing and PoC purposes. Email us at support@upstash.com . How many databases can I create? A free account can have 1 database. On a paid account, the first 10 databases have no per-database charge, and each additional database costs $0.50 per month, up to 100 databases. For more than 100 databases, contact support@upstash.com . The charge is calculated based on the number of active databases at the end of the month. What happens if I delete my database after 2-3 days? For Fixed plans, you are charged pro-rata for the days the database was active, even if you did not use it. For pay-as-you-go plans, you are only charged for actual usage during those days. How much is the price for bandwidth? For pay-as-you-go, monthly bandwidth is free up to 200GB. Beyond that, we charge $0.03 per additional GB. For Fixed plans, bandwidth is included up to your plan's limit. If your database is on the highest Fixed tier and exceeds its allowance, we will reach out with upgrade and Enterprise options. If we cannot reach you and usage continues, we reserve the right to charge bandwidth overages at our cloud provider cost rate. For high-volume use cases, VPC peering can reduce transfer costs. VPC peering requires an Enterprise contract. Contact support@upstash.com for details. Bandwidth pricing depends on the cloud provider's traffic fees, so it may change over time. If it changes, we will notify you by email. Can I purchase Prod Pack for any plan? Yes. You can purchase Prod Pack for any plan except the Free tier. You can enable it from your Upstash dashboard database details page. What is included in Prod Pack? Prod Pack includes uptime SLA, SOC 2 Type 2 report, advanced monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, and Datadog, Insights in the console, multi-zone high availability, and encryption at rest. Does enabling multi-zone high availability change my bill? Multi-zone high availability (part of Prod Pack) replicates write commands to the additional zones. Reads still hit a single replica, and command counts per write do not change, so it is only the extra write replication that adds bandwidth. On Fixed plans, commands are never metered, so multi-zone HA adds no command cost. The added write-replication traffic counts toward your plan's included bandwidth. On pay-as-you-go, a write is still billed as a single command no matter how many zones it is replicated to. The impact is on bandwidth, which is free up to 200GB per month and $0.03 per additional GB, so a write-heavy database may notice it there. What happened to the Pro 2K and Pro 10K plans? Pro 2K and Pro 10K were fixed-throughput dedicated plans, priced at $280/month and $680/month respectively. They are deprecated and have been replaced by pay-as-you-go, Fixed plans, and the Prod Pack add-on. If you are on a Pro plan, you can move to a Fixed plan for predictable pricing and add Prod Pack for multi-zone high availability and the uptime SLA. What is included in Enterprise subscription? Enterprise includes all Prod Pack features for all your databases. It also includes dedicated professional support, a dedicated technical account manager, unlimited databases, HIPAA compliance, VPC peering, SSO integration, and custom monthly or annual contract options. How is the Enterprise subscription priced? Enterprise pricing is custom and based on your requirements. For more information, email sales@upstash.com . Do you have the Professional Support plan? Professional support includes a dedicated service desk and a Slack/Discord channel with a committed response time SLA. Check Professional Support for details. Reach out via our contact page or social channels. Contact us Do you offer annual billing and ACH payment options? ACH is available only for annual payments from Enterprise plan customers. Contact us for more information. What if I'm on the Free plan and need just a few more builds this month? If you are on a Free plan and have used your monthly quota of free builds and updates, upgrade to the Starter plan. Does Expo store my credit card information? No, Expo does not. We use Stripe to handle payments, and they store your payment information. See how Stripe handles security for more information. Do you offer discounts for students, non-profits, or startups? No, we do not offer discounts at this time. Do you have Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) pricing? No, we do not offer PPP at this time. Do leftover monthly build credits roll over? No, credits do not roll over or accrue. At the beginning of each billing period, the included resources that come with your plan will be reset back to their original allotments. What are monthly active users (MAUs) and how are they calculated for updates? A monthly active user (MAU) is someone who downloads at least one update during the billing period. Multiple downloads by the same user count as a single MAU. Users who only check for updates but do not download anything are not counted as MAUs. Can my AI agent read this pricing page? Yes. This page is also available as plain markdown at expo.dev/pricing.md . Point Claude, ChatGPT, or another AI agent at that URL to compare plans and estimate costs for your team. Can I cancel at any time? Yes. You can cancel at any time. Your subscription will remain active until the end of your current billing period. What does it include? Yes, MongoDB Atlas offers a free-forever tier, the M0. Atlas’s free tier includes 512 MB of storage, 32MB of sort memory, and up to 100 operations per second. The free tier is a great starting point to learn about MongoDB and explore its capabilities in a fully managed cloud environment. Get started with a free tier → Atlas Free tier features and limitations → Guide: How to deploy a free tier cluster → How do I choose the right cluster tier for my application? Choosing the right MongoDB Atlas cluster tier for your application involves considering the application's workload, data size, and performance needs. Key considerations include: Free Tier (M0): Best for learning and exploring, with limited resources . Flex: Ideal for development and testing, offering the lowest cost option with certain feature limitations . Dedicated (M10 & M20): Suitable for pre-production and small, non-critical workloads. These tiers utilize shared vCPUs and support replica set deployments offering fully featured access to Atlas. Dedicated (M30+): Recommended for performance-critical and high-traffic workloads, supporting both replica sets and sharded clusters with fully featured access to Atlas with dedicated vCPUs. Clusters can always be scaled up from any tier as requirements expand. If unsure, MongoDB recommends starting with a lower tier and monitoring performance before adjusting. For all Dedicated tiers, use auto-scaling to adjust cluster tier and storage as workloads evolve. MongoDB Atlas costs are based on a pay-as-you-go model, influenced by several key factors: Cluster tier and type: The selected tier is the foundational cost driver. Higher tiers provide more dedicated resources and capabilities. Cloud provider and region: Costs vary slightly across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, and between different geographic regions. Data storage: Includes the size of your data and indexes. Data transfer (networking): Charges mainly apply to data moving out of your Atlas cluster (egress) or between different regions/cloud providers. Inbound data transfers are typically free. Free and Flex tiers are not charged for outgoing data. Backup services: Costs are based on the region and the monthly storage consumed by snapshots and oplogs for continuous backups. Note that backup services are not available for the Free tier. Add-on tools and services: Additional add-on tools and services contribute to the overall cost. Examples include but are not limited to: Atlas Stream Processing Dedicated MongoDB Search on Atlas Nodes Support subscriptions Premium Atlas Charts features Additional factors that can influence cost over time include: Fluctuations in usage Configuration adjustments Auto-scaling behavior New features Cloud provider price changes Atlas cluster configuration costs → Understand Your MongoDB Invoice → How do I manage and reduce MongoDB Atlas costs? Right-size clusters: Pause development or testing clusters when not in use. Alternatively, terminate them if no longer required. For Dedicated clusters, use auto-scaling to adjust cluster storage and/or tier based on real-time CPU and memory utilization. Optimize data management: Design efficient schemas and use strategic indexing to improve query performance while minimizing resource consumption. Regularly review clusters, databases, and collections to eliminate duplication, outdated data, and unused sample datasets. For Dedicated clusters, use Atlas Online Archive to tier infrequently accessed data, which will reduce primary storage costs. Minimize data transfer: Reduce data transfer costs by heeding the following best practices: Avoid queries that re-read client data or re-write existing cluster data. Use query projections to only retrieve necessary fields. Deploy applications in the same cloud region as the Atlas cluster. Enable network compression in client drivers to reduce data volume. Monitor & alerts: Regularly review spending patterns using the Billing Cost Explorer tool in Atlas. Additionally, set up billing alerts to be notified of unexpected cost spikes or when usage approaches predefined thresholds. Billing breakdown and optimization → How do I view a breakdown of costs and charges? The MongoDB Atlas UI's billing page includes a breakdown of costs. It provides: Invoices: Detailed historical breakdowns of charges including Cluster usage Storage Data transfer Backups Current balance: Outstanding balance and payment history Cost by project: A high-level overview of cost distribution across Atlas projects Cost visualizations: The following tools enable visualization and grouping of spend categories: Year-to-date usage chart Invoice charts Billing Cost Explorer Manage billing in Atlas → Does MongoDB Atlas offer any discounts? FAQ Frequently asked questions Is the Hobby plan really free? + Yes. The Hobby plan is hard-capped, needs no credit card, and never produces a surprise bill. You get 100K tool calls a month (up to 20K on Composio-managed apps), unlimited connections on your own apps, shared custom tools and MCP, 30 days of audit logs, and 3 team members. When you reach a cap, usage pauses until the next month or until you upgrade. What is the difference between my own app and a Composio-managed app? + With your own app you connect your own OAuth application or API keys and get the full 100K free tool calls a month. Composio-managed apps are shared OAuth apps we run so you can skip setup. You get 20K of that 100K free, shared across all managed apps. After that, Pro pays per call at the rates listed under Composio-managed apps, and provider rate limits still apply. They work in production but are not built for production scale, so move to your own app before you scale. How does the $29 Pro plan work? + Pro is $29 a month and includes usage credit that resets every month with no rollover. Past the included free amounts, overage bills on the rate card. You can set spend caps so you never get a surprise bill. What happens when I hit a limit? + On Hobby, usage pauses at the cap with no charge until the next month or until you upgrade. On Pro, you keep running and pay overage, and spend caps let you set a ceiling. Why do polling triggers cost more than realtime triggers? + With polling, Composio checks the provider on a schedule, even when nothing has changed. With realtime, the provider pushes each event to us. You still pay only for delivered events, never per poll. See how each type works . How are Instant Tools billed? + Use Instant Tools without separate API keys or subscriptions. Provider charges come from your Composio balance with 0% markup. Regular tool-call charges apply. Rates may change. With your own provider credentials, no Instant usage charge applies. Your provider bills your account, and regular Composio tool-call charges still apply. Read the Instant Tools guide . What are the optional add-ons? + Add-ons can be usage-based charges or one-time charges. Some usage-based add-ons apply automatically based on how a call runs, such as direct execution outside a Session, proxy execution, or running in the sandbox. Others you enable for security or compliance, such as zero data retention and IP allowlisting. Advanced white-labeling is a one-time per-connection charge. BAA is a per-call compliance add-on on Pro, and Enterprise includes it. How is Firewall billed compared with Sandbox LLM tokens? + On Pro, Firewall costs $0.50 credits per 1M tokens evaluated. Firewall is included on Enterprise. Sandbox LLM tokens cover model calls Composio runs for you in Sandbox. How do add-ons add up? + Most calls are just the base tool-call rate, or the app's rate on Composio-managed apps past the free allowance. Usage-based add-ons are small extras that apply only when a call actually uses that capability, so you never pay for one you are not using. BAA is a per-call compliance add-on on Pro, and Enterprise includes it. For example, a call that runs in the sandbox adds a small sandbox amount, and a proxy-execute call is still one tool call at the base rate with a small proxy add-on on top. On Pro you can set spend caps for metered usage, so metered usage never goes past a ceiling you choose. One-time add-ons are separate. What is proxy execute? + Proxy execute is an escape hatch for calling an API endpoint we have not wrapped as a tool, or for advanced request options a standard tool cannot express. Composio still handles auth, so you never touch raw credentials. It is billed as one tool call at the base rate plus a small proxy add-on for the pass-through, not as two separate charges. On Composio-managed apps, the managed rate replaces the base rate. Learn more . Can I avoid a surprise bill? + Yes. The Hobby plan is hard-capped, and on Pro you can set per-meter spend caps so spend never goes past a ceiling you choose. Still have questions? Reach out to support@composio.dev . Route Forwarding & aliases Add our MX records, and every address on your domain is yours. We have forwarded email since 2017, and 1.6M+ domains use us today. Unlimited aliases We never charge per alias or per user. Catch-all & regex Send every address, or any regex match, to the inbox you choose. Multi-recipient One alias can reach people, teams and webhooks. Disposable Turn off an alias without deleting its mail. → forward hello@studio.dev → you@gmail.com · 41ms Store Encrypted mailboxes According to our technical whitepaper, each mailbox is its own SQLite file, encrypted at rest with ChaCha20-Poly1305. The key is your mailbox password, and only you have it. IMAP · POP3 Works in Apple Mail, Thunderbird and phone apps. 10 GB pooled One storage pool for all your domains. Zero-knowledge Quantum-resistant encryption on every mailbox. Search & filters Search on the server, without downloading every message. ✓ imap.forwardemail.net · TLS 1.3 · mailbox sealed Send Outbound SMTP & newsletters Send as your domain from an app, a script or a campaign. We sign each message with your domain's DKIM key, so receivers can check it came from you. Unlimited outbound (reputation-based) Included on every paid plan from $3/mo. SMTP relay Works with any app or framework that speaks SMTP. Newsletters Each domain needs a one-time review, usually within 24 hours. Pre-warmed IPs We publish the IP addresses we send from. POST /v1/emails → 202 accepted · signed · tracked Sync Calendars, contacts & tasks Calendars, contacts and tasks use the open CalDAV and CardDAV standards. We added calendars in 2024 and contacts in 2025. Sign in with the same address and password as your mailbox. CalDAV Send and answer meeting invitations. CardDAV The same contacts on every device. VTODO Your Apple Reminders lists sync too. Open standards Export your data and leave any time. ✓ caldav.forwardemail.net · 3 calendars · 412 contacts synced Observe API, webhooks & reports Our REST API manages domains, aliases, messages, calendars and contacts. Webhooks post inbound messages to your app as JSON and retry up to 3 times on each delivery attempt. REST API Manage domains, aliases and messages, and download logs. Webhooks Each inbound email arrives as a JSON request. DMARC reports We turn the raw reports into a readable summary. Deliverability Analytics and alerts for each domain. POST https://your.app/hooks/mail → 200 · 1,284 events today Use Desktop, mobile and terminal apps We build our own apps for 6 platforms, from desktop and mobile to the terminal. The desktop and mobile apps work offline. Apple Mail and other mail apps work too. macOS · Windows · Linux Signed updates install themselves. Windows and macOS builds are code-signed. iOS · Android Native apps with push notifications. Terminal The forwardemail command, with desktop notifications. App Lock Turn it on to encrypt mail on the device with a PIN or passkey. ✓ update check → up to date · signature verified All-in-one, no add-on fees One dashboard for forwarding, mailboxes, sending and delivery. 99.99% Uptime 10 GB Pooled storage $0 Per alias Add your domain, prove you own it and route its mail. Send with SMTP or the API on any paid plan from $3/mo. New senders start at 300 messages a day (900 on the Team plan). Your daily limit grows as you keep paying and send clean mail. According to Gmail's sender guidelines , senders should keep their spam rate under 0.1%. We use the same rate. What is the prepaid platform usage, and how much do I need? The Apify platform has a number of services that are charged based on usages, such as Actors, proxies, data transfer, and storage. See pricing for the full list of platform services. Each subscription plan comes with a certain amount of prepaid platform usage that is used to pay for services. If your platform usage in a given billing cycle exceeds this prepaid amount, the excess usage will be added to your next invoice, and you'll get a notification. If you're on the free plan, your access to Apify's services will be blocked until the beginning of the next monthly cycle. Note that unused usage credits are not rolled over to the next billing cycle, and they expire at the end of the billing cycle. Can I try Apify for free? Absolutely! We offer a free plan that lets you use most of the features of the Apify platform, but with certain limits. No credit card is required. The free plan includes Apify Proxy, which is limited to use within the platform and does not extend to external clients. If you'd like a free demo of Apify's custom solutions, please contact us . Which plan should I choose? If you're unsure which plan is right for you, just pick the lowest-priced plan that has all the features you need. If you exceed the prepaid platform usage, you'll get a notification, and the excess usage will be added to the next invoice (see below for details). You can upgrade to a higher plan at any time in your Billing settings, and you'll only pay for the price difference. What is the pricing for Actors in Apify Store? Every Actor in Apify Store uses one of two pricing models, and each Actor's page states which one applies to it. Pay per event - you pay a fixed price for the events the Actor's developer defines, such as starting the Actor or returning a single result. Most pay-per-event Actors include the Apify platform usage in the event price, but some charge for it separately, so check the pricing section on the Actor's page. Pay per usage - the developer charges nothing on top, and you only pay for the platform usage consumed by the Actor's runs: compute units, data transfer, storage operations, and residential or SERP proxies. Both models draw on the platform usage credits included in your plan, and excess usage is charged to your next invoice. Reading from or writing to a run's dataset after the run finishes also counts as platform usage. The exact platform usage depends on the specific Actor, the type of job it performs, how often it runs, and for how long. The easiest way to find out the platform usage of an Actor is to perform a test run. You can then review your platform usage in your Billing settings and figure out the best subscription plan for your needs. For a full breakdown of both models, see Actors in Apify Store . If you need advice, please contact us . Can an AI agent pay for Actor runs without an Apify account? Yes. An autonomous agent with a crypto wallet can pay through the agentic payment protocols x402 and MPP , with no account and no human sign-up. The agent pays once at agi.apify.com , receives a temporary Apify API token with a fixed spend cap, and calls the Apify API with it like any other token. Each Actor run is metered against that prepaid balance, and unused balance expires with the token. Agents find the complete, current instructions, including supported chains, terms, and balance checks, at agi.apify.com/AGENTS.md . Can I upgrade, downgrade or cancel my plan? You can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel your plan at any time in your Billing settings. When you upgrade, your payment will be prorated, so you will only pay for the difference between the old and the new price, taking into account how much of the billing cycle has already passed. When you downgrade, there's no proration except for the unused platform usage that's rolled over to the new plan. If you decide to cancel, your subscription will last until the end of the current billing cycle. It won't be renewed after that. Note that you might still be charged for excess platform usage. What drives the cost of an Actor run? Most Actors in Apify Store use pay-per-event pricing. You pay the prices listed on the Actor's page for events such as returning a result. Pay-per-usage Actors and your own Actors bill platform usage instead, including compute units, storage, proxies, and data transfer. Some pay-per-event Actors charge both. You can check your daily usage chart on the Apify platform. What happens after I run out of prepaid usage? If you're a paying user, you can continue using the platform and will be charged for overage until you reach the usage limit configured in the billing. If you're on the free plan, you'll be blocked until the next billing cycle. What happens to my prepaid usage if I don't use all of it? If you don't consume all your prepaid usage, it disappears at the end of the billing cycle. Go to our pricing page to learn more about the prepaid usage of all Apify's subscription plans. Why do some of my Actor runs cost more than others? On a pay-per-event Actor, a run costs more when it returns more results or triggers more events. When you pay for platform usage, the cost depends on proxies, data transfers, memory, and run duration. It also depends on the number of retries when a request fails. How does Apify pay as you go work? If you're on one of Apify's paid plans, you can continue using the platform after reaching the limit by paying the rest as overage. That means you don't have to change your pricing plan to exceed the usage limit of your current plan. Does Apify offer any discounts for universities or nonprofit organizations? Apify offers discounts on its paid plans to both academic institutions and nonprofit organizations. Students are eligible for 50% off Starter, Scale, and Business plans, while nonprofits can get a personalized discount. Learn more at Apify for universities and Apify for nonprofits . Do startups get the same pricing as enterprise customers? Apify believes in encouraging startups to grow by using online data at scale. So we're giving a special 30% discount on our Scale plan to startups. Learn more at Apify for startups . I would like to develop Actors. What should I do? Apify Academy is a free course that shows you how to start developing Actors on the Apify platform. You can also find more information in the Apify documentation . Couldn't find something? Inngest handles the orchestration — retries, concurrency, throttling, scheduling, and observability — all without workers or queues on your end. FAQ What counts as one "execution"? An execution is metered per function run and per step inside that run. A function with 5 step.run() calls uses 6 executions total — 1 for the run, 5 for the steps. If you're estimating usage, count steps, not just runs. How many executions does a typical workflow use? It depends heavily on step count. A simple 2-3 step job might use 3-4 executions per run. A multi-step AI agent with tool calls, retries, or sub-agent handoffs can use significantly more — often 10+ executions per run. Model your usage against your actual step count, not the headline execution number. What happens when I exceed my plan's included executions? On Pro, overage is metered at tiered rates that decrease as volume grows (from $0.000050 down to $0.000015 per execution, based on current published rates). On Free, there's no metered overage — execution pauses once you hit the free quota, and you'll need to upgrade to resume. Which limits are most likely to affect me? Executions are the most common constraint for most accounts. Concurrency, seats, workers, span data, and events each have their own separate limits and overage rates, but they typically become relevant only at higher scale or with specific usage patterns (e.g., many team members, high trace volume). Can my bill change from month to month? Yes. Because execution volume, concurrency, and several other dimensions are each billed independently, your bill can vary if usage spikes on any one of them — not just total execution count. What's included versus billed as an add-on? Core execution, concurrency, seats, and workers are part of your plan's base allowance and overage rates. Advanced observability and HIPAA compliance are separate paid add-ons, not included in the base Pro, Business, or Enterprise price. How does Inngest's pricing model compare to Temporal's or Trigger.dev's? The three vendors bill on different units. Temporal charges per "action" — a workflow start plus one charge for every step (called an activity) inside it, so cost rises directly with how many steps a run has. Trigger.dev charges a flat per-run fee plus metered wall-clock compute time, so a slower step (a bigger file, a slow API call) raises the bill even at the same step count. Which vendor is cheapest for my workload? It depends on how many steps your typical run has and how long each step takes to execute — that's the number to check before comparing sticker prices, not the headline monthly rate. A third-party cost comparison modeled 500,000 runs/month at 4 steps each against each vendor's published rates and found the ranking can flip depending on step count and compute duration per step — so we'd recommend running your own numbers against your actual workflow shape rather than relying on any one published comparison, including this one. Why might the same workload cost different amounts on different platforms? Because "cost per run" depends on three separate variables that each vendor weights differently: step count, compute time per step, and whether overage is metered continuously or in fixed tiers. A workflow with few, fast steps and one with many, slow steps won't rank vendors the same way. Can I switch plans later? Yes. You can upgrade from Free to Pro or Business at any time, and switch to Enterprise once you need custom scale, SAML, or dedicated support. Plan changes take effect immediately and prorate the current billing cycle. Can I self-host Inngest? Yes. Inngest is open-source and can be self-hosted. The cloud product adds managed infrastructure, observability, and reliability on top — but the core engine is yours to run. I have other billing questions. How do I get in touch? Email us at support@inngest.com or open a support ticket from the dashboard. Pro and Enterprise customers get faster SLAs on billing and account questions. Clever Cloud automates every step, from git push to production, enabling teams to deliver faster, with peace of mind, and without depending on complex scripts, or on a single provider . Whether you deploy on public cloud, on-premise, or in an isolated environment, the experience remains the same. Try it now or talk with our team. Try for free Request a demo Déploiement Git natif : push et go We believe application deployment can – and should – be simpler. With Clever Cloud, a simple git push is enough: the application goes live automatically, without manual intervention. No need for complex configuration files or custom scripts. With its built-in build detectors, Clever Cloud automatically recognizes the language and framework of your project, with no extra setup required. You remain free to adjust the parameters as needed. Auto-scaling: real-time resource adjustment Is your application facing traffic spikes? No worries: auto-scaling is available natively. You can configure minimum and maximum instance ranges so the platform dynamically adapts resources to the load. As a result, your teams no longer waste time calibrating infrastructure, and your application stays performant – even during unexpected traffic surges . It is also a lever for cost optimization: auto-scaling prevents permanent over-allocation of resources – you only consume what you need, when you need it . Environment management: simple and secure isolation Testing, staging, production… each environment has its own specifics. Clever Cloud allows you to isolate them cleanly, with dedicated environment variables, distinct security settings, and a clear separation of databases and associated resources. You can clone an existing environment, simulate production behaviors, and test without risk of regression. This approach makes collaboration between teams smoother, while reducing the likelihood of human errors. Seamless CI/CD integration: compatible with your tools Clever Cloud does not impose its own CI/CD pipeline. You can integrate it with GitHub Actions, GitLab, or any other tool via our Clever Tools CLI or API. At each git push, the platform can automatically build and deploy your application without complex configuration. You remain free to choose your level of automation. Flexible deployment: the same experience everywhere Deployment simplicity doesn’t stop at the public cloud. Clever Cloud can be deployed in on-premise , air-gapped , or multi-cloud environments , while keeping the same tools and interface. Whether your infrastructure runs on OVHcloud , Scaleway , Cloud Temple , Outscale , Oracle Cloud , or your own servers , you keep a single point of entry. The deployment experience remains the same: same interface, same API, same CLI. Clever Cloud enables you to: Deploy in a fully controlled environment, with specific compliance or network constraints; Avoid vendor lock-in by keeping the freedom to switch providers without redesigning your delivery process; Reuse your existing tools and skills across any target infrastructure. No reconfiguration, no extra tooling required: you administer all your environments the same way, whether on our public cloud or on your own machines. High availability: automatic recovery of machines Clever Cloud is designed to keep your services online, regardless of technical failures. In the event of a crash or malfunction of a virtual machine, our orchestrator automatically restarts the instance – with no manual action required – ensuring immediate service continuity. This mechanism is at the core of our high availability and resilience approach: your applications are distributed redundantly, and resources are automatically redeployed to maintain performance and a seamless user experience. Deployment process Scalability and performance Environments and configuration Integration and CI/CD Multi-cloud and on-premise Deployment history and traceability Can a deployment be triggered on every push to a specific branch? Yes. Clever Cloud deploys automatically on every git push. To target a specific branch (e.g. main), you need to configure your repository accordingly or use a CI/CD tool to ensure deployments are triggered only from selected branches. Can I run a command after a deployment? Yes. Clever Cloud allows you to configure several hooks via environment variables, for example: CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK=”npm run build”: runs a command right after compilation and before cache generation, and CC_PRE_RUN_HOOK=”php artisan migrate”: runs before the application starts. These hooks let you automate tasks such as database migrations, front-end builds, or other specific actions, without manual intervention. See the documentation for details. How can I manage secrets (API keys, tokens…) in an automated deployment? Secrets can be defined through environment variables in the console or via the API/CLI. They are isolated per application and encrypted at rest. Can I monitor the impact of auto-scaling in real time? Yes. The console shows the evolution of instances and CPU/RAM metrics, and you can configure custom alerts through Grafana. Does auto-scaling also apply to databases? Not at this time. Automatic scaling is currently reserved for applications. Databases (via Materia) rely instead on high-availability mechanisms such as replication, backups, and leader/follower setups. Can I clone an environment with its data? Clever Cloud allows you to clone an application. For databases, duplication is done via export/import or snapshot, and APIs are available to automate this process. Cloning an application does not automatically replicate its data. To reproduce a full environment, you need to export/import the associated database. How can I manage different configurations (e.g. staging vs production)? Use environment variables specific to each application, separate Git branches, or distinct .clever.json files if needed. What are the best tools to integrate Clever Cloud into a CI/CD pipeline? GitHub Actions and GitLab CI are the most commonly used and documented solutions with Clever Cloud. You can also integrate Clever Cloud with other CI/CD tools via the Clever Tools CLI or the API, to automate deployments, manage secrets, and handle applications. Does Clever Cloud provide an API to manage deployments? Yes. The public API lets you create/deploy applications, manage environment variables, track logs, and more. It is used in production by many customers to industrialize their workflows. Can I run Clever Cloud on my own infrastructure? Yes. Clever Cloud can be installed in on-premise or air-gapped environments to meet strict requirements for security, sovereignty, or connectivity. This model is particularly suited to sectors with strong regulatory constraints (public sector, healthcare, defense, industry), or organizations that want to retain full control over their infrastructure. On-premise deployments use the same automation mechanisms, the same interface, API, and tools (CLI, monitoring, IAM). Management remains unified across environments. A technical validation is carried out with our teams before any deployment, to ensure compatibility (network, storage, virtual machines, security, etc.). Can multiple cloud providers be combined with Clever Cloud? Yes. Clever Cloud can be deployed on different compatible infrastructures: public cloud, on-premise hosting, partner environments, or air-gapped setups. This allows you to administer all your environments through a unified interface and tools, without specific adaptations for each provider. Which infrastructure providers are compatible with Clever Cloud? The platform can be deployed on providers such as OVHcloud, Scaleway, Cloud Temple, IONOS, or Oracle Cloud, provided that the environment is compatible (VMs, networking, low-level access). A technical validation is performed on a case-by-case basis. Can I audit what was deployed, when, and by whom? Yes. Clever Cloud keeps a detailed history of activities in the Activity section of the console, or via the API. Each event shows the date, the type of action (Console, Git, Monitoring…), the author (member of your organization), and the associated commit. Redeployments performed automatically by the platform (e.g. after scaling or maintenance) are also clearly indicated, without a human actor attached. This system provides useful traceability, even if it does not constitute a full user-level audit trail. To achieve certified user-level traceability (e.g. with strong identification), you can rely on a CI/CD pipeline or an external logging/auditing tool. Learn more about seed funding Frequently asked questions Are applications for the DigitalOcean Startups program currently open? Applications for our current cohort are temporarily paused as we prepare to launch an updated program experience in early 2027. When will the new DigitalOcean Startups program launch? The new program is scheduled to launch in early 2027. I am a current Hatch / Startups program participant. How does this affect my benefits? Active program members are not affected by this pause. Your existing DigitalOcean credits, 1-on-1 technical advisory sessions, and partner perks remain fully active through the duration of your original program term. You can continue accessing your benefits via your founder dashboard or by contacting startups@digitalocean.com. Are you still accepting new accelerator, VC, and incubator partners? Yes! We actively welcome new venture partners and portfolio managers. If you manage an accelerator, VC fund, or startup community, please reach out via startups@digitalocean.com to discuss co-marketing opportunities and early partner access for 2027. What is DigitalOcean Startups? DigitalOcean Startups helps developers create, launch, and scale their startups. This includes a range of perks to get you started, including 12 months of DigitalOcean credits to easily deploy and scale your infrastructure. Why is DigitalOcean doing this? We want to empower the startup community. We always strive to support and show love to our community. We want it to be easy for you to have access to our resources. Who is eligible for DigitalOcean Startups? How do you select DigitalOcean Startups members? We prioritize AI-native startups. Service-based startups (consulting services, web/app development services, marketing agencies, etc.) are not eligible. New applicants are evaluated using the following criteria: Must have raised $10m or less. Must have a company website, and an email address associated with the company website. Must create a registered DigitalOcean team account with a business/company email (not a personal email account). How do I know if my accelerator/incubator/VC firm has a relationship with the DigitalOcean Startups? Please see our portfolio partner list . You can ask your program manager if you have a partnership with DigitalOcean Startups. How many credits do I get? DigitalOcean awards startups credits through approved DigitalOcean Startups partners. To learn more about your eligibility award level, please contact your program manager at your DigitalOcean Startups Partner. What if I have already received credits for my startup? This program is for new startups that have not used prior credits with DigitalOcean. How do DigitalOcean credits work? You will be given a pre-determined amount of credits as set out in your onboarding email to be used over the term of the program with Qualifying Program Services. Participants generally are entitled to a $10,000 monthly limit (and charges apply for any use in a month exceeding this amount). When accepted into the program, what types of services can I use with my credits ("Qualifying Program Services")? As of May 13, 2026, you may use your credits on any DigitalOcean services, except as to the following: GPU Droplets NVIDIA H100 GPU Kubernetes Bare Metal GPUs Dedicated Inference Serverless Inference, Third-party AI models hosted outside of DigitalOcean Infrastructure (including commercial/frontier models, including but not limited to Anthropic and OpenAI) Paperspace Machines Cloudways services Any other charges passed through to third-party providers outside of DigitalOcean's infrastructure This set of credits are referred to as “core” credits. GPU credits are a separate benefit and will not be covered by the core credits received when initially accepted into the program. Acceptance into the program does not ensure entitlement of GPU credit benefits, and are made available to select customers after review of their GPU credit application and infrastructure needs. Not sure if a certain product is covered by your credits? Reach out to startups@digitalocean.com and we'll get back to you as soon as possible. Do DigitalOcean credits cover GPU Droplet usage? DigitalOcean Startups core credits do not cover your GPU Droplet usage, and may only be used with Qualifying Program Services. Your account's payment method will be charged for usage of GPU Droplets and any other services not appearing on the Qualifying Program Services. Can you help migrate my customers from other public clouds to DigitalOcean? Yes, we have migration plans, technical assistance, and credits available to make it easy for your clients. How do I receive access to the DigitalOcean Startups perks? You can access DigitalOcean Startups' perks through the Welcome Kit that you receive when you're accepted into the program. What happens if I go over the monthly credit limit? If you go over the monthly credit limit, you will be charged for the additional usage for that month. Do I need to be a DigitalOcean customer to sign up for DigitalOcean Startups? Before applying for DigitalOcean Startups, you must create a new DigitalOcean team account for your startup with 1) the corporate email address associated with your company domain and 2) a valid credit card. You can learn more about DigitalOcean team accounts here . For security reasons, applicants must include a working website and matching corporate email address. Can I transfer my DigitalOcean credits? No. The DigitalOcean credits are designed to help you scale your infrastructure and are not transferable. If you do not use the credits, they will be forfeited. Are there any other limitations on how I use DigitalOcean credits? Yes. Program credits may only be used for Qualifying Program Services, which excludes GPU Products. Additionally, you cannot use any program credits for the mining of cryptocurrency (e.g. bitcoin mining). You can also not use the DigitalOcean credits for services in a manner that consumes excessive network capacity, CPU cycles, or disk IO, or that are AI model inference services hosted by third party vendors. If you do, use of services other than Qualifying Program Services are subject to additional charges, and DigitalOcean may end your participation in the DigitalOcean Startups program. Please review the DigitalOcean Startups Terms of Service for complete program terms. I haven't been able to spend all my credits. Can I get an extension? The DigitalOcean Startups program does not grant extensions. FAQs How are searches counted? Only successful searches are counted toward your monthly searches. Cached, errored, and failed searches are not. The number of results returned per response will not affect the number of credits used—responses with 100 results or empty result sets will both count as 1 search. Can we upgrade, downgrade, or cancel at any time? Yes, you can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel your plan at any time without any restrictions. What happens if I cancel before my plan expires? If you cancel before your plan expires, you can continue to use your remaining searches until the renewal date. After that, your plan will not be renewed. What happens when I upgrade my plan? When you upgrade your plan, you'll only pay the difference between your current plan and the new one. Your renewal date will remain the same. What happens when I downgrade my plan? When you downgrade your plan, you'll keep your current renewal date, and your subscription will renew at the lower plan rate. Any remaining searches from your previous plan will be added to your 'Extra Credits' balance. What happens if I run out of searches in a month? You can set your plan to Automatic Early Renewal. It will trigger an early renewal once you've used all your searches. You can toggle the Automatic Early Renewal anytime by visiting this page . You can also renew your plan manually. In both cases, your searches will be fully replenished, your renewal date will be updated, and your searches will reset at the start of the new billing cycle. What's your refund policy? We offer a full refund within 7 days of the date you subscribed to a plan unless you've used more than 20% of your searches. Apple pay requires a Safari browser. For additional payment options, including wire transfer, purchase orders, and ACH, please contact us . Note that when you add a card, we may send a temporary pre-authorization request to the issuing bank. This pre-authorization charge is immediately released by DigitalOcean but may take a few days to clear from your card depending on the bank. When will my card be charged? DigitalOcean billing cycles are monthly. Typically, on the first day of each month we invoice and automatically charge your account's primary payment method for the previous month's usage. In some cases, we might charge if your usage exceeds a threshold . You can also login and self pay the balance at any time. Am I charged when I enter my credit card? No. Your card is only charged at the end of the billing cycle or upon exceeding a usage threshold. Pre-authorization charge: When you add a card, we may send a preauthorization request to the issuing bank. This is to verify that the card being added has been issued by the bank and that they will authorize any charges in future. These temporary pre-authorizations are typically $1 but can vary in range and are immediately canceled by us. Depending on your bank, it might take a few days for the charge to clear from the card. Will taxes be included in my monthly invoice? We're required by law to apply taxes in some countries. Click here to learn whether we collect taxes in your country, what the tax rate is, etc. How do I destroy my resources? Check out the docs to learn how to destroy Droplets , Kubernetes clusters , Managed Databases clusters ( PostgreSQL , MySQL , Caching ), Spaces , Volumes , Firewalls , and Load Balancers . Can I be notified if my bill exceeds a threshold? Yes, you can set up billing alerts and we will email you if the monthly spending exceeds an amount you specify. How does the $5 free credit work? Your card will be charged only after you have utilized the free credits or after the credit expiration period. For example, if you received a $5 credit for 90 days, then that $5 credit is automatically applied to your account. If you spend $3 in that timeframe, your card will not be charged. If you spend $10, the $5 credit will be fully utilized, and your card will be charged only $5. Since the credit is valid for 90 days, you won't be able to use any remaining credit after the 90-day period expires. What's the price for the Marketplace 1-Click Apps? We charge you for the underlying compute on which the 1-Click Apps runs. How do I remove my card from the account? To remove a saved payment method, visit the products billing page and click the … menu of the payment method, then click Delete. In the Confirm Delete Card window that opens, click Delete to remove the card. You cannot remove the default payment method on the account. Can I prepay for my resources? If you are interested in prepayment for resources, contact our experts . Can I have a refund? We do not offer refunds. If there are extenuating circumstances, contact support. Still have questions? Have a complex setup or additional questions around pricing? Contact our sales team to get more information on DigitalOcean pricing. Not included in Included in Security Questionnaire Help Not included in Not included in Included in Included in Frequently asked questions Can I cap my usage so my bill doesn't run over? Yes. Spend caps are on by default on the Pro Plan. You can turn spend caps off for usage beyond the Plan limits to pay as you grow. I'm worried I could end up with a huge bill at the end of the month. Spend caps are on by default and you need to toggle them off from your dashboard to enable pay as you grow pricing. When will I be billed? Our Pro Plan is charged up front, and billed on a monthly basis. Additional usage costs are also billed at the end of the month. Does Supabase charge sales tax, VAT or GST? Supabase applies sales tax, VAT, GST, and other indirect taxes where required by law, based on your billing address. For more details, see our Billing FAQ . Are you going to change your pricing in the future? Pricing may change in the future. As a team of developers, we are committed to keeping our pricing as developer friendly as possible. What happens if I cancel my subscription? The organization is allocated credits for unused time during the billing month. Those credits can be used for other projects. How can I track my usage? You can track your organization's usage at any time on the usage page in the dashboard, which shows how each project is tracking against your plan's limits. Your upcoming invoice on the billing page updates as you go, and organizations on the Pro Plan or above can use the Spend cap to control costs. What if I need one project for development and one for production? You can create two projects, one for development and one for production — the Free Plan includes two free projects. You can also use Branching , available on the Pro Plan and above, to run a separate development environment off your production project. Can I self-host Supabase for free? Yes, you can use the Docker setup or the Supabase CLI . Supabase Studio is also available in the Docker setup. Can I pause a free project? Yes, you can pause a project at any time. Our Free Plan gives you 2 free projects, but you can have as many paused projects as you want. Just pause and unpause them as needed. Can I purchase Supabase through AWS Marketplace? Yes. If your organization has an AWS spend commitment (such as a PPA or EDP), you can buy Pro or Team through AWS Marketplace so eligible Supabase spend counts toward that commitment. Billing details and plan management then run through AWS, and Spend Cap is unavailable for AWS-managed organizations. Learn more on our AWS Marketplace page , or go straight to the public listing . James Hawkins Co-founder Our pricing is designed to make you happy Here's what you should know about our pricing: We don’t have loss-leader products that will go up in pricing later or get retired. We aim to match the cheapest competitor at every scale. Tell us if we're not! (Note: This doesn't include your buddy's two-person startup.) We have significant revenue and are default alive . We don’t rely on investors to grow, and we’re stable. This goes a long way to avoiding the average dumb VC-backed company stuff — like running out of money or selling to a lame bigger company. We have an open source product too. It is MIT licensed if you want to use it in a big organization that isn’t ready to move to PostHog Web yet. If this makes you happy, just start here: Get started - free No credit card required Pricing FAQ How do I know how much PostHog will cost? The easiest way is to sign up, set your billing limit to $0 (if you expect to go over), and install PostHog. You'll get an accurate projection after just a few days. You can also read our doc on estimating usage and costs . Do I pay anything for stored data (events, exceptions, replays, logs, etc.)? Not for most products. You pay for what you capture, ingest, or sync in a given month, and storing it costs nothing extra. The exception is Logs custom retention: if you keep logs or traces longer than the 14-day default, each GB costs $0.05 for every month you keep it. How long does PostHog retain data (events, recordings, logs)? Events are retained for 1 year on free plans and 2 years on pay-as-you-go plans. Platform packages let you set a custom retention policy to keep events for longer: up to 3 years on Boost, 5 years on Scale, and 7 years on Enterprise. For more information on data retention, see the events data retention docs . Recordings on the free plan are retained for 1 month. On the pay-as-you-go plan, recordings are retained for 90 days. The Boost and Scale add-ons can increase this to up to one year. The Enterprise add-on can increase retention to 5 years. Logs are retained for 14 days by default. You can set custom retention per service or per source. Custom retention bills for the data you keep, not this month's usage: each GB costs $0.05 for every month you keep it, until it expires. Your Logs billing limit stops ingestion but doesn't cap custom retention, and custom retention can't have a limit of its own. What happens after the data retention period elapses? Any data stored for more than the retention period may be permanently deleted from our systems. Is there a free trial on paid plans? We have a generous free tier on every paid plan so you can try out all the features available on PostHog before paying (though you will need to enter your credit card to unlock those features). If you have additional needs, such as enterprise features, please get in touch with our sales team . What currency are your prices in? All prices are in US Dollars (USD), excluding taxes. Do you offer a discount for non-profits? Yes in most cases! Create your account, contact the sales team for help with some basic details on your organization. We will then apply a discount. Are there any minimums or annual commitments? Nope. We can, however, offer annual commitments (for example, to maintain pricing) if you need them as part of an enterprise agreement. How does PostHog's pricing work? PostHog has per-product usage-based pricing. This means you only pay for what you use, such as events captured, sessions recorded, and flags requested. PostHog is free to use and each product has a generous free monthly allowance (1M events for analytics, 5K session replays, 1M feature flag requests, and more). There is no minimum spend or annual contracts needed and you can set billing limits so you're never surprised. Which plan is right for me? For nearly everyone, the pay-as-you-go plan is the right choice. It unlocks all of the features of PostHog and remains free if you stay within the limits each month (which you can set billing limits to do). What happens if I hit or go over the free limit? On the pay-as-you-go plan, we charge based on usage for everything above the free allowance. On the free plan, any additional events are permanently dropped and feature flags will return a default quota limited response. Do free tier limits reset every month? Yes. Every month, your usage is reset and you get another 1M events, 5K session replays, and more to use. Unused free tier limits do not rollover. Logs custom retention has no free tier. It bills for the data you keep, not this month's usage. Can I set a billing limit? Yes, you can set a billing limit for most of PostHog's products separately in your organization's billing settings . Logs custom retention can't have a limit, and your Logs limit doesn't cap it. Check out our doc on billing limits and alerts for more information. What happens if I hit my billing limit? If you've set a billing limit and your usage hits it, any additional events are permanently dropped and feature flags will return a default quota limited response. PostHog will never charge you more than what you've set as your billing limit. The exception is Logs custom retention, which your Logs limit doesn't cap. How is usage calculated? Usage is calculated on a per-product level. Events for product and web analytics, recordings for session replay, requests for feature flags and experiments, exceptions for error tracking, responses for surveys, synced rows for sources, messages for workflows, GB ingested for logs, and GB-months kept for Logs custom retention. Do multiple projects share usage and free allowances? Yes. Billing is organization-wide, so usage from all your projects is combined into one bill with one free allowance. Adding projects doesn't add extra free usage. The free plan includes one project, and paid plans include more. See how to organize projects for our recommended development, staging, and production setup. How can I manage my spend? You monitor your usage and set billing limits on the billing page in-app. This shows how much you've spent, projected spend, and a billable usage dashboard. Many products, like product analytics and feature flags , also have docs on cutting costs. Can I cancel my plan at any time? Yes, you can cancel your plan by setting a billing limit at any time and we'll only charge for what you use. Billing limits don't cap Logs custom retention. If you have an accidental spike , talk to us and we'll help you sort it out. Is PostHog cheaper than competitors? Usually, yes, and often by a significant margin. Because PostHog provides multiple products teams need, we're able to charge less than competitors. We aim to be the cheapest option for each product compared to major competitors. Beyond the all-in-one advantage, most competitors offer time-limited free trials (typically 14-30 days) with restricted features; PostHog's free tier doesn't expire, includes full access to most features, and resets every month, no credit card or sales call required. You can read how we stack up against competitors like Amplitude , Mixpanel , Heap , FullStory , Hotjar , GA4 , and a lot more in our comparison blogs . What do I get with PostHog that I wouldn't get paying for multiple separate tools? A lot less headache, mostly. All your data lives in one place so you don't need to jump between tools or piece them together to do analysis. With PostHog, you can go directly from a funnel to a replay to an error trace instead of context switching to piece together what actually happened. You just need to install a single SDK, manage a single bill, and sign a single contract (if you're into that sort of thing). If you need a BAA for HIPAA compliance, it's one conversation instead of five. Your procurement team will genuinely thank you. When does billing start? Usage starts being tracked as soon as you sign up for PostHog, but you aren't billed until 1 month later. For example, if I signed up on April 6th, my first month would be billed May 6th. How often am I billed? You are billed once a month, on the same day each month. What payment methods does PostHog accept? PostHog accepts credit or debit cards processed through Stripe. If you want to pay via invoice, you can contact the sales team for help . Do you support invoicing or purchase orders? Yes, but you need to make an upfront credit purchase which can be done by contacting our sales team . Does PostHog have any setup fees or hidden costs? No. Our pricing is fully transparent. Can I use PostHog completely free forever? Yes, as long as you stay under the free tier limits. Many of our users have used PostHog for free for years. Do I need to pay for everything or only certain products? You can choose what products you use and you don't need to pay for anything you don't want. You can set billing limits for the products you don't want to use to be extra safe too. PostHog's products still work if you only use them individually. Does PostHog offer annual commitment discounts? Yes. PostHog does offer bigger discounts for annual commitments above a certain spend. See our doc on pre-paid plans for more. Have another pricing-related question? Ask PostHog AI or talk to a human . Shameless CTA If nothing else has sold you on PostHog, hopefully these classic marketing tactics will. Apply now You'll need a PostHog account first A hedgehog in a suit laughing: haha, business! FAQ Can I use my credits on all PostHog products? Almost all of them. From September 14, 2026, startup credits can no longer be used towards bills incurred on AI tools such as PostHog Desktop, the PostHog Slack app, Replay Vision, PostHog AI, and Inbox. This is due to the prohibitive and unpredictable nature of token-based pricing. Credits still cover everything else, including AI observability and the context warehouse. Can I use credits to claim a BAA under the Boost plan? Credits cannot be used to claim a BAA under the Boost plan due to legal risk. If you’d like to claim a BAA, you can instead contact us to discuss options . Credits can be used towards other aspects of the Boost package. Why can I not use my credits on AI features? From September 14, 2026, startup credits can no longer be used towards bills incurred on AI tools such as PostHog Desktop, the PostHog Slack app, Replay Vision, PostHog AI, and Inbox. Token-based pricing makes the cost of these tools prohibitive and unpredictable, which makes them harder for us to subsidize. If you joined PostHog for Startups before September 14, 2026, usage before this cut-off can still be paid with credits. How do I apply? Just sign up to a paid plan in PostHog (you're only charged for usage) and then fill in this form . Apply from a PostHog account that uses your company email address. We will apply the credit automatically if you're eligible. If you're accepted into the startups program, we will notify you by email. Who's eligible? Your company needs to be less than 2 years old and have raised less than $5m funding. You need to have signed up any time from Jan 1st 2023 onwards, and your PostHog account needs to use your company's email domain. Applications from personal email addresses, like gmail.com or outlook.com, are not accepted. Can I get credits more than once? No. We issue startup credits only once per founder and once per organization, whichever comes first. For example, if you already got credits for one startup, you can't claim them again for a new company or a new PostHog organization. We always issue credits at PostHog's discretion, and we can decline an application or remove credits if it doesn't meet these rules. What if we don't have a company email domain yet? You need one to apply, but you don't need credits to start. Every PostHog product has a monthly free allowance , so you can build on PostHog for free and apply for the program once you have a company domain. I signed up before this deal launched, can I still get it? Yes, but only if you signed up after Jan 1st 2023. If your startup meets the eligibility criteria but you signed up to PostHog before Jan 1st, we won't apply the credits but are still happy to enroll you in the rest of the program. I use another tool, like Amplitude or Pendo. Can I migrate that data to PostHog? Yes, you can migrate your data from another tool to PostHog using our migration guides , which cover how to migrate from tools such as Amplitude, Pendo, Plausible, Mixpanel, Heap, LaunchDarkly, Google Analytics, and more. Do you offer onboarding help, to make sure I get everything set up correctly? Yes. By joining the startup program, you'll already get access to our startup newsletter full of tips and tricks for getting the most out of PostHog, as well as invites to our exclusive events. If you need more help, you can purchase a 30-minute onboarding call with our team , or explore custom service packages . Please note that PostHog credit can not be used towards these services. Can I get this deal if I'm part of YC? We have a separate deal for YC folks – check out Bookface . No, they don't stack! What if I go over the $50k limit? At that point you can move onto another PostHog plan . What happens at the end of the 12 months? At that point you can move onto another PostHog plan . You'll continue to be considered part of the startup program in terms of invites to office hour events, and other perks. How do I get the Incident.io/Speakeasy/Depot discount? Once you're accepted into the PostHog for Startups program, we'll email you with details on how to get the partner benefits. What level of customer support do I get? Do I get a dedicated account manager? PostHog is run by a small team and, as such, we're only able to offer support to paying customers. Organizations which are part of our startup plan are therefore not eligible for high priority customer support, and only qualify for normal priority and community support. You also don't get a dedicated account manager, customer success manager, or sales contact. This is still the case even if you apply your credits towards a platform package, such as the enterprise add-on. If you want one-to-one help getting set up, you can purchase a 30-minute onboarding call with our team .
